article.articleSummary: Judy, a polio-affected chimpanzee rescued from wildlife trafficking, died after more than 30 years at Ol Pejeta Conservancy's Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary in Kenya. Born in 1983 and believed to have originated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, she was rescued at about age 10 and arrived with lifelong effects of polio on her right foot. Despite disability, she adapted using her strong front limbs to move and lived among other chimpanzees and caregivers. Judy was a devoted mother to Oscar (born 1997) and spent her later years with companions Alley and Poco. Veterinary staff described her as a symbol of resilience, strength, and kindness, highlighting the importance of sanctuaries in providing lifelong care to trafficked chimpanzees. Her story underscores ongoing need for protection of wildlife and rescued animals.

The disease, Ebola haemorrhagic fever, originated in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with a fearsome outbreak in the DRC ongoing for months. Unlike the 2014 Lagos import via a Liberian vectored Ebola, this instance is an imported case into Nigeria. The episode underscores that, had the index traveler’s passport history been carefully perused and established that she had been to Congo before travelling to Uganda, she would have been quarantined in Abuja before trouble reared its head. Now the country is scrambling to manage what it could have prevented. Some social media voices frame the return as a political ploy, but health authorities face an imported Ebola case requiring careful handling.

triage.headline_ja: エボラが再来
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ流行に関連し、ナイジェリアへ14年ぶりに輸入症例が発生。IHR基準（重篤性・異常性・国際伝播・渡航制限リスク）を複数満たし、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はナイジェリアへの輸入エボラ症例だが、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。感染源であるDRCでの進行中のエボラ流行について明示的言及があるためDRCを含めた。渡航歴管理の不備（検疫漏れ）が指摘されており、管理体制の課題が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Lung Collapse Due to Tuberculosis Sequelae.
article.articleSummary: In Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, 27-year-old Anh Thanh presented with cyanosis, cough, and shortness of breath. CT revealed severe airway disease with complete collapse of the right lung due to scarring and obstruction of the right main bronchus from sequelae of treated pulmonary tuberculosis three years earlier. TB-induced bronchial fibrosis can trap mucus and impair airflow. After multidisciplinary discussion, surgeons performed an end-to-side bronchial anastomosis rather than the standard end-to-end resection; they created an opening in the healthy bronchus to attach the obstructed segment, reestablishing ventilation and preserving lung tissue. The operation required meticulous dissection near major vessels and one-lung ventilation during anesthesia. Three days post-op, the patient was extubated; within a week his oxygenation normalized and symptoms resolved, and he was discharged. The team urged TB survivors to monitor respiratory symptoms after treatment and seek timely care if dyspnea, wheeze, or chest pain occur.

triage.headline_ja: 結核後遺症による肺虚脱
triage.triage_reason: 単一症例の臨床報告であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や集団感染、異常な流行学的事象を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 結核既往患者の個別症例（外科治療報告）であり、公衆衛生イベントとしての新規性・集団性はない。

article.articleHeadline: Boy co-infected with three bacteria and a virus.
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, a 2-year-old boy, Sơn, presented with high fever, cough, tachypnea, and chest indrawing. Initial testing showed respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection with radiographic signs of bilateral bronchovascular thickening, diagnosed as RSV pneumonia and acute nasopharyngitis. Subsequent PCR revealed co-infection with Bordetella parapertussis, Haemophilus influenzae, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. The child developed fast breathing (56 breaths/min) and SpO2 92% on room air, required oxygen via face mask, and intensive respiratory monitoring; six days later he recovered from cough, no respiratory distress, and was discharged. The report notes rising pediatric respiratory illness in autumn at Tam Anh General Hospital Hanoi, with September counts of 792 respiratory cases and 362 hand‑foot‑mouth disease; early October estimates show about 25% more respiratory cases (~990) and 40% more hand‑foot‑mouth (~507) than September. Parents are advised to monitor breathing, fever, feeding, and alertness, seek care for red flags, and avoid self-prescribing antibiotics.

triage.headline_ja: 男児が3種の細菌とウイルスに重複感染
triage.triage_reason: 単発の小児症例報告であり、RSVや市中細菌による呼吸器感染の季節的増加を示すのみで、国際的拡大や渡航・貿易制限のリスク、特異な公衆衛生上の脅威は認められない。
triage.notes: 季節性の小児呼吸器疾患・手足口病の増加傾向が言及されているが、本記事は個別症例報告が主体であり、集団発生や異常な病原性を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Why China and Pakistan Need a Cross-Border Animal Disease Notification Protocol
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease SAT1 outbreaks loom across China–Pakistan borders. Pakistan’s Punjab province reported FMD signals on Oct 17, with officials pledging zero tolerance for reporting delays. The cross-border gap is acute: formal WOAH reporting requires 24-hour notification but relies on a country’s detection and willingness to disclose. Iraq detected SAT1 in Jan 2025; by May 2025 it appeared in the WOAH database, and by Mar 2026 Iran was affected, with Pakistan and Afghanistan deemed likely entries—risk peaking around Eid al-Adha. Pakistan’s dairy sector had urged faster vaccine development since vaccines cover only serotypes O, A, Asia-1. In China, SAT1 outbreaks emerged in Xinjiang and Gansu by late March 2026, prompting culling, tighter border controls, and emergency vaccine approval. Vietnam warned of very high entry risk in April due to illegal movements. The piece advocates a China–Pakistan cross-border notification protocol to accelerate data sharing, complementing vaccines and trade, noting existing accords lack operational triggers.

triage.headline_ja: 中国とパキスタンに越境動物疾病通知プロトコルが必要な理由
triage.triage_reason: 口蹄疫(FMD)SAT1型が中国・パキスタン・イラン等で越境拡大しているが、本疾患は主に家畜に影響し人間への公衆衛生上の直接的脅威は限定的であるため、経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本記事は家畜の口蹄疫(FMD SAT1型)に関する越境報告体制の論説であり、人間の公衆衛生への直接影響は記載なし。中国(新疆・甘粛)で実際の発生が確認されているため含めたが、パキスタン・イラン・イラク・アフガニスタンは対象国リスト外、ベトナムは「侵入リスク警告」のみで実発生の記載がないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: More than 40,000 hand, foot, and mouth disease cases in Ho Chi Minh City, warning of the risk of dangerous complications in children.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) outbreaks in Vietnam surged in 2026, with Ho Chi Minh City reporting over 40,000 cases since January and 40,446 through week 41, and Hanoi recording over 6,000 cases across 126 wards/communes. HFMD is caused by enteroviruses, notably EV71, and can progress rapidly to severe neurologic and cardiopulmonary complications, including encephalitis, meningitis, myocarditis, pulmonary edema, hypertension, heart failure, and shock, potentially fatal without timely care. In Ho Chi Minh City, week 41 incidence rose 32.2% versus the four-week average, signaling ongoing transmission in childcare settings. Typical progression begins with fever, fatigue, sore throat, and poor appetite, followed by mouth ulcers and vesicular rashes on hands and feet; severe signs include fever ≥39°C, dehydration risk, lethargy, vomiting, rapid breathing, or seizures. Precautionary guidance emphasizes hydration, soft foods, hygiene, and prompt medical evaluation; Vietnam licensed an EV71 vaccine in 2026 to bolster prevention.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市で手足口病が4万例超、子どもの重篤合併症リスクを警告
triage.triage_reason: 手足口病（EV71含む）がホーチミン市で4万例超、ハノイでも6千例超と急増し、脳炎・心筋炎等の重篤合併症が報告されており、重症度・流行継続性の観点からWPRO基準に複数該当し、当局の警告（社会的関心）も確認されるため。
triage.notes: 手足口病はベトナムで季節性に流行する既知の疾患だが、今回は症例数の急増（週41で前4週平均比32.2%増）と重篤合併症（脳炎・心筋炎等）への警告が強調されており、フルリスク評価での経過確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Many children with Japanese encephalitis develop severe complications
article.articleSummary: As of 24 October 2026, Thanh Hoa National Children’s Hospital in Vietnam reports multiple pediatric Japanese encephalitis cases with severe complications. The Infectious Diseases Ward has admitted seven children since early October; several arrive in coma or with seizures, and some develop focal paralysis or require intubation and mechanical ventilation. One 10-year-old patient is severely ill with Japanese encephalitis, brain edema and pneumonia, under intensive care and respiratory support; improvement is ongoing but brain swelling persists. Doctors note that most affected children are not fully vaccinated against Japanese encephalitis. There is no specific antiviral treatment; vaccination remains the most effective preventive measure. Parents are urged to vaccinate on schedule, and to seek prompt medical care for high fever, headache, vomiting, seizures, neck stiffness or altered consciousness to reduce mortality and long-term neurological sequelae.

triage.headline_ja: 日本脳炎に罹患した多数の小児が重篤な合併症を発症
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムの小児病院で日本脳炎の重症例が複数報告されているが、同国では季節性・地域流行性の既知疾患であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 日本脳炎はベトナムで季節性に発生する既知の蚊媒介性疾患であり、ワクチン未接種児童での重症化が報告されている。ヒト-ヒト感染はなく、国際的拡大リスクは低い。

article.articleHeadline: Tay Ninh records 10 deaths due to rabies.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam, as of 24 October 2026, shows 9 dog rabies cases across 7 communes/wards and 10 human rabies deaths across 10 communes/wards (Lương Hòa, Hưng Điền, Mỹ Hạnh, Đức Lập, Mỹ An, Lộc Ninh, Hòa Khánh, Truông Mít and the wards Thanh Điền, Gò Dầu). In the past week, one additional dog case was recorded, bringing canine infections to 9, while no new human deaths occurred this week; however the cumulative mortality underscores ongoing risk. Preventive measures emphasize full vaccination of dogs and cats, and strict animal management to avoid roaming. After dog or cat bites or scratches, promptly wash the wound with soap under clean water and seek medical care for timely rabies vaccination; avoid unproven treatments. Rabies remains deadly once symptoms appear, highlighting the need for vaccination and proper post-exposure management.

triage.headline_ja: タイニン省で狂犬病による死亡者10人を記録
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・タイニン省で狂犬病による死亡者が累計10人に達し重症度は高いが、同国では狂犬病が風土病的に発生しており異常性や国際的拡大リスクは低いため、経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はベトナムで風土病的に発生しており、ヒト-ヒト感染がないため国際的な公衆衛生リスクは限定的。ただし犬の予防接種率や咬傷後対応の遅れによる死亡が継続している点は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: A Hanoi manager flew to Saigon to date a female college student; after just meeting on Oct. 20, the next day both were infected with HIV.
article.articleSummary: A Hanoi-based manager and a university student in Ho Chi Minh City were diagnosed with HIV within 24 hours after meeting on Oct 20. Both tested HIV-positive at a Ho Chi Minh City prevention clinic on Oct 21 following unprotected sex over their year-long relationship. The student reported fatigue and lymphadenopathy; rapid tests were confirmed by follow-up testing. The manager disclosed he has a wife and daughter in Hanoi, raising concern about potential exposure to family. Health authorities stress honest discussions of sexual health, regular testing, and protection. The article advises consistent condom use for vaginal or anal sex, routine testing after high-risk behavior, and HIV prevention options such as PEP (started within 72 hours of exposure) and PrEP for at-risk individuals, alongside vaccination and prompt medical care for symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ハノイの管理職男性がサイゴンへ飛び女子大学生とデート、10月20日に出会った翌日、両者がHIV感染と判明
triage.triage_reason: 個別症例の報道であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性、国際的拡大リスクは認められない個人間感染事例であるため。
triage.notes: HIVの既知感染症であり、個人の性行為による感染事例の報道。公衆衛生上の警戒事象ではなく、健康啓発目的の記事と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: BJMC, Sassoon to use advanced sequencing to detect drug-resistant TB
article.articleSummary: Pune-based BJ Medical College (BJMC) and Sassoon General Hospital (SGH) will for the first time conduct targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) to identify drug-resistance mutations in tuberculosis (TB) patients. The initiative aims to improve diagnosis and enable doctors to tailor treatments for drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). tNGS sequences selected gene regions connected to resistance, delivering rapid, multi-gene mutation profiles and addressing limitations of phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing and narrower molecular tests. The study will start next month, with 48 samples isolated, including both drug-sensitive TB patients and DR-TB patients at SGH. WHO has recommended tNGS to detect drug resistance and guide clinical decisions. BJMC participates in the Indian Tuberculosis Genomic Surveillance (InTGS) Consortium. Findings will be shared with the governments of India and Maharashtra. tNGS can test multiple drugs in a single assay and may be more cost-effective for comprehensive DST, especially depending on drugs tested.

triage.headline_ja: BJMCとサッスーン病院、薬剤耐性結核検出に高度シーケンシング技術を導入
triage.triage_reason: 新規の診断技術導入に関する研究報告であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常な感染拡大を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事は薬剤耐性結核の検出技術（tNGS）導入に関する医療機関の取り組みを紹介するもので、アウトブレイクや症例急増の報告ではないため対象国locationも計上しない。

article.articleHeadline: As malaria, dengue cases persist, doctors say only community-level interventions can help
article.articleSummary: Malaria and dengue persist in Mumbai, with Neelam Singh’s 19-year-old son diagnosed with malaria and a platelet count of 40,000, spending four days at Kokilaben Hospital before recovery. Across Criticare Asia Multispeciality Hospital chains in Mumbai, more than 20% of 550 beds are occupied by malaria and dengue patients. Doctors note dengue risk during the day from mosquitoes breeding in stagnant water and malaria risk at night, underscoring the need for community-level state action rather than individual measures. Construction sites have created stagnant puddles that fuel mosquitoes; BMC says fogging is ongoing and workers are being trained to identify breeding sites, though some residents fault hygiene and garbage in slums. Officials report a drop in vector-borne disease cases in the first half of October versus September. Separately, worsening air pollution (PM2.5/PM10) aggravates respiratory symptoms; wearing an N95 and limiting outdoor activity during peak smog is advised.

triage.headline_ja: マラリアとデング熱の流行が続く中、医師らは地域レベルの介入のみが効果的だと指摘
triage.triage_reason: ムンバイでマラリア・デング熱の流行が継続中だが、季節性の媒介動物感染症であり新規性や国際的拡大の懸念は低い。地域の公衆衛生対応として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: マラリア・デング熱はインド（ムンバイ）で毎年発生する季節性の媒介動物感染症であり、10月前半には症例数が減少傾向との報告あり。記事は公衆衛生対策（地域レベルの介入）の必要性を論じる内容で、新興感染症や国際的な脅威には該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Health Minister Arunraj Reviews Dengue Prevention Measures in Otteri
article.articleSummary: Chennai, Tamil Nadu — Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj inspected a monsoon medical camp at S.S. Puram, Otteri, to review fever cases and dengue prevention in ward 75 of Thiru.Vi.Ka. Nagar. He sought details from the city health officer on fever cases and dengue infections reported in S.S. Puram and asked whether mosquito-control workers were inspecting the area. The minister distributed pamphlets on dengue prevention and urged residents to remove discarded items that can collect rainwater. He inspected rooftops and advised keeping water storage containers covered and clearing unused articles to cut mosquito-breeding sites. A motor pump on First Cross Street to drain rainwater was reviewed, with orders to ensure street re-laying after the monsoon. He sampled pongal at Amma Unavagam and directed repairs to the purified drinking water unit. Accompanied by MLA M.R. Pallavi and other officials.

triage.headline_ja: 保健大臣アルンラージ氏、オッテリでのデング熱予防対策を視察
triage.triage_reason: 通常の季節的なデング熱予防活動の視察報道であり、異常な感染拡大や重症例急増を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: モンスーン期の通常の蚊媒介疾患対策・行政視察の記事であり、症例数や死亡者数などの具体的な規模を示すデータは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Old City to Rajendranagar, Hyderabad loses sleep to mosquitoes
article.articleSummary: Hyderabad's Tolichowki and other Old City localities report an evening-to-night surge in mosquitoes, prompting residents to rely on nets, coils, and electric devices as GHMC fogging struggles to curb biting. Officials warn mosquitoes may be developing resistance to insecticides; fogging targets adults, while larvae and pupae in drains persist. The spread affects Tolichowki, Shah Ali Banda, Falaknuma, Fateh Darwaza, Golconda, Mallepally, New Malakpet, Red Hills and Rajendranagar. Dengue fears persist: 266 dengue cases Jan 1–July 13, with 127 laboratory-confirmed, down from 570 (2025) and 821 (2024) for the same period. Aedes aegypti, the dengue/chikungunya vector, bites mainly by day; evening/night swarms are largely Culex, which can carry lymphatic filariasis and Japanese encephalitis. Weaker monsoon rains reduced stagnant-water pools. GHMC’s “one ward, one day” fogging/anti-larval drive covers 30 circles, 150 wards; the city has had no elected council since Feb 10.

triage.headline_ja: 旧市街からラジェンドラナガルまで、ハイデラバードは蚊の大発生で眠れぬ夜
triage.triage_reason: 蚊の大量発生とデング熱・日本脳炎等のベクター媒介疾患リスクが報じられているが、デング熱症例数は前年・前々年より減少傾向にあり、重大な公衆衛生危機とは言えず情報も限定的なため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱症例数は2024年・2025年同時期より減少傾向。蚊の殺虫剤抵抗性の懸念と選挙未実施による行政対応力低下（GHMC評議会不在）が指摘されているが、現時点で重大なアウトブレイクの証拠はない。

article.articleHeadline: Don't take monsoon fever lightly: Three infections lie behind a single symptom—Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika; how to identify them?
article.articleSummary: Monsoon-season in Gurugram, India, brings Aedes mosquitoes breeding around homes in water-filled containers, boosting dengue, chikungunya, and Zika transmission. The three infections share fever, headache, and muscle pains in early days, making clinical distinction difficult. Dengue is often marked by severe body aches, retro-orbital pain, and a rapid drop in platelet count, with abdominal pain, vomiting, or bleeding in severe cases. Chikungunya features intense joint pain—especially in ankles, wrists, knees—that may persist for weeks or months, sometimes hindering movement. Zika typically causes milder illness with rash and red eyes; pregnant women face risks to fetal brain development, so prompt testing is advised. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment and laboratory confirmation; treatment is supportive. Do not self-medicate with aspirin or ibuprofen until dengue is ruled out; maintain fluids. Seek urgent care for bleeding, persistent vomiting, or severe abdominal pain.

triage.headline_ja: モンスーンの熱を軽視するな：一つの症状の裏に潜む3つの感染症―デング熱、チクングニア熱、ジカ熱、その見分け方は？
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の一般的な健康啓発記事であり、異常な流行や新規の公衆衛生上の脅威を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: インド・グルガオン（ハリヤナ州）におけるモンスーン期の蚊媒介感染症に関する一般的な医療啓発記事。症例数や異常な流行拡大についての具体的データは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Tick-Borne Diseases Growing Concern
article.articleSummary: Tick-borne diseases (TBDs) are a growing concern in India, with Tamil Nadu an important endemic region. In Tamil Nadu, vectors Haemaphysalis intermedia, H. bispinosa and Rhipicephalus sanguineus transmit zoonoses such as Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD), Indian tick typhus, and Lyme disease (Nilgiris). Nationally, over 125 tick species exist; notable zoonoses include Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF), KFD, Indian tick typhus, Lyme disease, and Q fever, with outbreaks in Karnataka, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Seroprevalence of Borrelia burgdorferi reaches 19.9% in parts of Karnataka and 18% in Arunachal Pradesh; CCHF outbreaks have caused human fatalities in Gujarat and Rajasthan. A unified One Health surveillance platform is urged to coordinate human, animal and environmental monitoring. Acaricide resistance in Rhipicephalus microplus and Hyalomma anatolicum reaches 68–78%, with residues contaminating milk, meat and the environment. Most tick burden originates in cattle sheds; improved shed management and vaccines are proposed.

triage.headline_ja: ダニ媒介性疾患の懸念が拡大
triage.triage_reason: インド各州におけるダニ媒介性疾患（CCHF、KFD等）の流行状況に関する総説的記事であり、新規の急性アウトブレイクを示すものではないが、継続的な曝露リスクが示唆されるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はインド複数州（タミル・ナードゥ、カルナータカ、グジャラート、ラージャスターン、ヒマーチャル・プラデーシュ、アルナーチャル・プラデーシュ）における既知のダニ媒介性疾患（CCHF、KFD、ライム病、Q熱、インドダニチフス）の流行状況をまとめた総説記事であり、特定の新規アウトブレイクを報告するものではない。One Healthサーベイランス体制の必要性が強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: LUCKNOW NEWS: Dengue is now spreading rapidly, with 20% more patients in just seven days.
article.articleSummary: Dengue is spreading rapidly in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, driven by post-monsoon waterlogging from heavy rains. In the second week of October, 69 new dengue cases were reported; Mon–Fri of this week added 90 more. Over two weeks, Indiranagar has 38 cases and Chandernagar 36, with Sarojininagar, Chinhat and Tudiyanj also affected. In Indiranagar, cases rose from 14 in week one to 24 in week two; Chandernagar from 13 to 23; Aliganj from 13 to 17. Health authorities have mobilized daily survey teams and mobile units to test and distribute medicines. Dengue wards have been expanded: Balrampur Hospital (20 beds); Bhau Rao Deoras Civil Hospital (10 beds + fever desk); Lokbandhu Hospital (6 beds); Indiranagar Municipal Community Health Center (3 beds). Control room: 0522-2622080. Preventive measures urged: eliminate standing water, wear long sleeves, use nets, dispose of waste, and seek early testing.

triage.headline_ja: ラクナウニュース：デング熱が急速に拡大、わずか7日間で患者数が20%増加
triage.triage_reason: インド・ウッタルプラデーシュ州ラクナウでのデング熱の季節的流行であり、地域内での患者数急増は見られるが、国際的拡大や渡航制限等のIHR基準には該当しない。地方当局が対応中で情報も限定的なため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドで毎年季節的に流行する蚊媒介感染症であり、本記事はラクナウ市内の局地的な患者数増加と地方保健当局の対応状況を報じるローカルニュースである。重症度や死亡例の詳細は記事に記載がなく不明。

article.articleHeadline: Indian American physician Navin Shah commits $525,000 to infectious disease program in Pune
article.articleSummary: Indian American physician Dr. Navin C. Shah commits $525,000 over five years to establish the Navin C. Shah Infectious Disease Program at BJ Government Medical College in Pune, Maharashtra, in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University. The initiative funds research, medical education, faculty and student exchanges, and patient care, with a patient care fund and a focus on tuberculosis, HIV, and antibiotic-resistant infections affecting economically disadvantaged communities. The program builds on a 2003 Johns Hopkins–BJ partnership, including early HIV mother-to-child transmission research with nevirapine. Four Johns Hopkins faculty visits to India and two BJ faculty visits to the United States are planned, plus an annual seminar starting December 4. BJ Medical College-affiliated hospital has about 1,800 beds, highlighting the program’s aim to expand activities beyond conventional grants and strengthen Indo-U.S. collaboration in infectious disease care and training.

article.articleHeadline: Beyond case management: Why dengue prevention needs stronger vector-management systems
article.articleSummary: India approved its first dengue vaccine in July 2026, with the Union Health Ministry backing vaccine rollout alongside vector-control and case management. Dengue prevention now hinges on Integrated Vector Management (IVM), targeting Aedes aegypti before illness occurs. The mosquito bites early morning and late afternoon, breeds in and around homes, and eggs can survive eight months; hatching occurs in 7–10 days. Delhi reported by early October 2026 more than 3.18 crore home visits and breeding in over 1.89 lakh homes, illustrating data-driven prioritization. Dengue case counts show 289,235 in 2023; 121,824 in 2025; 23,952 in the first half of 2026. Pupae counts help identify productive containers; resistance to DDT documented in 2023 Indian studies, guiding insecticide choices. IVM combines source reduction, larvivorous fish, larvicides, fogging, and Indoor Residual Spraying; construction sites, Mumbai laws, and Ahmedabad inspections highlight cross-sector responsibility to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Kolkata sees surge in hand, foot and mouth disease in children
article.articleSummary: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is surging in Kolkata, with scores of children affected and some adults ill. Hospitals report four children in the last fortnight. Physicians note a shift in symptoms this year: extremely itchy rashes spreading to the body and lower back, recurring after apparent recovery. Lesions appear on hands, palms, elbows, underarms, back, hips, knees, feet, and inside the mouth; some cases resemble chickenpox. Most cases are self-limiting and resolve in about a week, with fever, mouth ulcers and painful eating common. Management is supportive: paracetamol for fever/pain, adequate fluids, and antihistamine lotions or IV fluids for dehydration. Preventive advice includes hand hygiene, cleaning surfaces, and keeping infected children at home; seek care for dehydration, persistent fever, drowsiness, or worsening symptoms. Surge observed over the past 10 days; Aug cases earlier.

In parallel, AIIMS-Nagpur is converting its Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory into an Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (IRDL) at Rs 17 crore, funded by ICMR-DHR, expanding bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology testing and broadening infection coverage; it should be functional within three months. The upgrades reflect concerns over rising human-animal interfaces due to deforestation and climate change. Emphasis is on integrating syndromic and genomic surveillance, including whole-genome sequencing, for early detection of mutations and emerging pathogens. AIIMS-Nagpur’s microbiology department already contributes to national surveillance and has helped grant PCR-testing status to more than 250 labs.

article.articleHeadline: Nasal congestion and headache: How to tell the difference between the effects of weather changes and a viral infection?
article.articleSummary: Weather changes do not directly introduce respiratory viruses; in India, seasonal shifts influence the environment, behavior, and exposure to respiratory viruses, according to Dr. Samir Bhatia in the Times of India. Temperature fluctuations between outdoors and air-conditioned spaces can dry the nose and throat, while changes in humidity and air quality may irritate airways, causing mild congestion, throat itch, or headaches. Allergens such as pollen or dust can trigger allergic rhinitis with sneezing, runny nose, and congestion. Signs suggesting a viral infection include fever, chills, body aches, fatigue, worsening sore throat, or a persistent cough, and recent contact with a sick person is an important clue; however, symptoms alone cannot confirm the cause, as some viral infections (including influenza) can occur without fever.

article.articleHeadline: Reported Echinococcosis in Xinjiang Peaked in 2017 and Fell to a 2022 Low,
article.articleSummary: Xinjiang, China reported 20,302 echinococcosis cases from 2010–2024, peaking in 2017 and declining to a 2022 low, based on the China Infectious Disease Surveillance and Reporting System. Joinpoint regression showed an APC of 8.91% (2010–2017) followed by -12.56% (2017–2024); overall AAPC was -2.42% (CI -5.80 to 0.83%), with results sensitive to model specification. Monthly notifications shifted over time. In forecasting, five time-series methods were evaluated for 2020–2024 using 2010–2019 training data under a fixed-origin setup and four error metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE, sMAPE. In fixed-origin, LSTM yielded the lowest errors (RMSE 47.08, MAE 39.24, MAPE 105.91%, sMAPE 46.07%). Under expanding-window rolling-origin, SARIMA delivered the best RMSE/MAE/sMAPE, with LSTM comparable. Conclusion: forecast performance depends on the evaluation framework, not just epidemiology.

Birds such as pigeons, sparrows, and other wild birds can harbor the organism, often without symptoms. article.articleHeadline: AI Model Reads Chest Scans to Tell Fungal Infection and Tuberculosis Apart
article.articleSummary: In HIV/AIDS patients with pulmonary infection in Southeast Asia and southern China, distinguishing Talaromyces marneffei from Mycobacterium tuberculosis is difficult due to overlapping symptoms. A Nanning study enrolled 380 patients (2018–2025): 203 TB and 177 T. marneffei, with etiologic confirmation by Xpert MTB/RIF, culture, histopathology; fungal cases by microscopy, culture, or molecular testing. A three-model approach included: (1) clinical predictors—fever, CD4 count, platelets, hemoglobin, diabetes, hypertension; fungal cases had median CD4 17 vs 127 cells/μL; RF AUC 0.856. (2) radiomics on 1,561 features (11 retained) with XGBoost AUC 0.866. (3) a 2.5D deep-learning model using seven CT slices and ResNet-18, achieving slice AUC 0.865 and patient-level AUC 0.885 (MIL strategies; SVM on aggregated features). The fusion model reached test-set AUC 0.931 and specificity 0.981. Grad-CAM visualizations showed network attention in representative cases.

article.articleHeadline: Unusual lipid pattern emerges in patients with Brucella spondylitis
article.articleSummary: Brucellosis patients, especially those with Brucella spondylitis, show a distinct lipid pattern in a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted in Inner Mongolia at two infectious disease hospitals in Hohhot and Xing’an League from May 2022 to March 2024. Of 702 brucellosis patients, 296 (42.2%) had spondylitis. HDL-C levels were positively associated with Brucella spondylitis (OR 1.992; 95% CI 1.229–3.228). Three derived lipid–inflammation indices were negatively associated: monocyte-to-HDL ratio (MHR) OR 0.298; atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) OR 0.446; and atherogenic index (AI) OR 0.819. Associations were linear on restricted cubic spline analysis and consistent across age, sex, disease stage, and comorbidities. Sensitivity analysis with multiple imputation supported robustness. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis suggested lipid-derived indices could aid risk stratification for spinal involvement in brucellosis, though causality cannot be established due to the cross-sectional design; prospective validation is needed.

article.articleHeadline: Measles on the rebound; vaccines remain the ultimate defense! City CDC reminds →.
article.articleSummary: Measles rebound in Qingdao, China prompts warnings from the City CDC that vaccination remains the ultimate defense. Measles is a highly contagious acute respiratory infection caused by the measles virus, with environmental viability limited by sunlight and heat but capable of persisting under cold conditions; winter–spring remains peak season. Two-dose measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination provides the best protection and also safeguards against mumps and rubella, underpinning the National Immunization Program. Vaccination coverage has driven down incidence, but boosters remain essential. For children, the schedule requires one dose at 8 months and a second at 18–24 months; adults over 18 may vaccinate voluntarily and at their own expense with informed consent. Citizens are urged to trust vaccines, complete the immunization program, and protect infants from infection.

article.articleHeadline: Polymicrobial Bile Infections Linked to Sepsis Risk and Antibiotic
article.articleSummary: Polymicrobial infection in acute biliary infection is linked to higher SIRS and sepsis risk and greater antimicrobial resistance, reported from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University in Yinchuan, China. In a retrospective study of 208 patients treated with ERCP or PTGD (Aug 2020–Aug 2023), 61 (29.3%) had polymicrobial bile cultures versus monomicrobial infections. Escherichia coli was the most common pathogen overall, with polymicrobial cases showing a higher proportion of Gram-positive organisms. Multivariate analysis found polymicrobial infection independently predicted both SIRS and sepsis, while antimicrobial resistance was more frequent in the polymicrobial group—driven largely by E. coli resistance, though resistance did not independently drive SIRS/sepsis. A history of biliary surgery emerged as an independent risk factor for polymicrobial infection, suggesting early risk stratification and empirical therapy considerations. Limitations include retrospective, single-center design and bile-culture–based sampling.

article.articleHeadline: Single Amino Acid Contact Drives Assembly of Newcastle Disease Virus
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease virus (avian paramyxovirus type 1) assembly of inclusion bodies hinges on a single contact: glutamine 370 in nucleoprotein binds serine 254 in phosphoprotein. Li et al. (Shandong Academy of Agricultural Sciences; China; Belarus) map this motif, suggesting a target for antivirals. Using TEM, immunofluorescence, viral titration, co-immunoprecipitation and structural modeling, the study analyzes velogenic F48E9 and lentogenic LaSota strains, which form inclusion bodies in chicken embryo fibroblasts, mouse embryonic fibroblasts and HeLa cells, with virions visible in chicken cells. Replication occurs in all three cell types; mouse cells show lower levels, and F48E9 yields more inclusion bodies in mouse cells. In HeLa cells, inclusion bodies nucleate near the nucleus at ~6 hours post-infection, grow by 12 hours, and fuse by 24 hours; sizes are small (<3 μm^2), medium (3–8 μm^2), and large (>8 μm^2). DF-1 transfection identifies the minimal viral components required for assembly.

article.articleHeadline: Mango Compound Mangiferin Shows Multi-Stage Activity Against Toxoplasma
article.articleSummary: Mangiferin, a mango-derived C-glucosylxanthone, shows multi-stage activity against Toxoplasma gondii. In work from Henan Medical University in Xinxiang, China, published in Frontiers in Microbiology, mangiferin inhibits parasite growth in cultured human foreskin fibroblasts, rapidly alters tachyzoite morphology, and prolongs survival of mice infected with virulent RH strain. In vitro, host cell viability remained >90% at 320 μM (10–320 μM tested); plaque assays showed no plaques at 320 μM and reduced plaque numbers/areas at 160 μM (significant differences vs vehicle; p=0.0006 for plaque count; p=0.0013 for plaque area; Dunn’s test mainly vs control at 320 μM). Extracellular tachyzoites rounded within 30 minutes, with more pronounced effects at higher concentrations; SEM after 2 hours confirmed rounding and spherical forms at 320 μM. This is initial evidence rather than a therapeutic breakthrough. Toxoplasma gondii is an obligate intracellular parasite causing toxoplasmosis, posing higher risk to immunocompromised and pregnant individuals; current therapy (pyrimethamine+sulfadiazine) is limited by toxicity.

article.articleSummary: COVID-19 infections rise across China in October 2026, driven by Omicron NB.1.8.1 sublineages. Hospitals brace for winter with potential triple epidemic of COVID-19, influenza, and RSV; China CDC data show ongoing spread. Immunity from prior infections wanes. Public health responses include updated masking guidelines, air purifiers and medical-grade air filters, fortified antivirals and fever meds stocks, and reinforced indoor ventilation. Authorities urge vulnerable populations to get updated vaccines immediately. Routine genomic sequencing continues to rapidly detect new mutations.

article.articleSummary: Weather cools and influenza activity rises in parts of China, signaling the peak season is November to March and the best time to vaccinate. article.articleHeadline: How China Tracks COVID-19 Cases and Outbreaks
article.articleSummary: China's COVID-19 monitoring has shifted from zero-COVID mass testing to risk-based testing and routine respiratory surveillance. As of August 2026, China reported 771,000 confirmed COVID-19 cases, 640 severe cases, and six deaths, noting these figures do not capture all infections. National guidance no longer mandates universal nucleic-acid screening; testing is guided by symptoms, exposure, setting, and risk, with weekly testing in elder-care and social-welfare facilities during outbreaks and prompt testing for fever or respiratory symptoms. China CDC's sentinel acute respiratory-infection system now includes SARS-CoV-2 in its panel, testing outpatient, emergency, and hospitalized patients for influenza-like illness and severe acute respiratory infection to track COVID-19 alongside other pathogens. The current framework relies on targeted testing and surveillance rather than widespread isolation, and historical zero-COVID rules (the 20 Measures and 10 Measures) should not be treated as current nationwide requirements.

article.articleHeadline: Lab study finds extremely low salivary transmission of Oropouche virus in
article.articleSummary: Oropouche virus, the cause of Oropouche fever across Latin America and the Caribbean, is transmitted mainly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis, with occasional evidence for mosquitoes. A 2024 surge in cases spread beyond the Amazon Basin, linked to a reassortant strain, 240023. A laboratory vector-competence study tested Culex quinquefasciatus and Aedes albopictus for replication and transmission of BeAn 19991 and 240023. In Cx. quinquefasciatus, the outbreak strain replicated less efficiently at low doses, but overall vector competence was extremely low (0-1% shed infectious virus in saliva), arguing against sustained transmission. Aedes albopictus showed higher infection with 240023, but overall transmission remained limited (0-6.4% in legs or saliva). Differences by mosquito genotype: Salvador City vs Houston lines; infectious saliva detected only in Salvador line (up to 20%), never in Houston. Conclusion: the 2024 expansion is unlikely due to adaptation in these mosquitoes; other vectors or field dynamics may be involved.

article.articleHeadline: 11 municipalities in Minas Gerais report cases of human scabies
article.articleSummary: Scabies outbreaks were reported in 11 municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil, including Alfenas, Belo Horizonte, and São Gonçalo do Pará. The State Health Secretariat (SES-MG) announced on 20 October 2026. Scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) is a skin disease transmitted mainly by prolonged direct skin contact, less often via shared clothing or bedding. It is not a nationally notifiable disease; outbreaks are monitored by municipalities. A defined outbreak is cases in a geographic area. Prevention includes hand hygiene, regular bathing, laundering of clothes and linens, and avoiding sharing items until control measures are in place. Washable items should be cleaned in hot water and ironed; non-washables can be sealed in plastic bags for at least three days. Treatment uses topical creams or prescribed medications; transmission generally stops about 24 hours after starting treatment, though itching can persist weeks. Seek a Basic Health Unit if symptoms appear, especially with others who are itchy.

article.articleHeadline: An 86-year-old woman dies after being bitten by a mosquito: 'She had no health problems'.
article.articleSummary: An 86-year-old woman, Granada Romero Ruiz, died in Seville, Spain, in July 2024 after contracting West Nile virus from a mosquito bite, spending nine days hospitalized. She reportedly had no prior health problems. The La Puebla del Río municipality condemned the death and urged reinforced mosquito control and public-health measures. West Nile virus is transmitted mainly by Culex mosquitoes, with birds as natural reservoirs. Infections are often mild or asymptomatic: about 80% asymptomatic, ~20% flu-like, and fewer than 1% progress to severe neurological disease such as meningitis, encephalitis, or spinal involvement. Elderly individuals are at higher risk. There is no antiviral treatment or licensed human vaccine; prevention centers on reducing mosquito exposure (repellents, screens, protective clothing) and eliminating standing water. The virus circulates across Europe, Africa, and the Americas; Brazil has reported human infections.

article.articleHeadline: A tick with a star on its back may threaten dogs and cats; learn how to identify.
article.articleSummary: Lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum) poses a risk to dogs and cats in North America, and may be mistaken for Brazilian star-tick species such as Amblyomma sculptum. Identification is challenging; the adult female’s white star-like dorsal mark aids recognition but is not definitive, and local tick species in Brazil can differ in disease transmission. The tick can transmit Ehrlichia ewingii, associated with ehrlichiosis in dogs, while some star-tick species in Brazil are linked to Rocky Mountain spotted fever in humans. Regular post-outdoor inspection of pets is advised, focusing on ears, head, between toes, armpits, groin, abdomen, neck, and around the collar, and bedding. If found, remove with fine-tipped tweezers by pulling firmly without twisting or squeezing; monitor for signs such as apathy, loss of appetite, fever, or swelling and seek veterinary care if symptoms emerge. Prevent year-round with veterinarian-recommended antiparasitics and environmental maintenance.

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 Infects 108 Inmates at Rio Verde's CPP - Fala Canedo
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 outbreak at Rio Verde's Provisional Prison (CPP) in southwestern Goiás, Brazil, has infected 108 inmates among 531 detainees and 28 staff. Response includes isolating positive and symptomatic individuals, reinforcing mask use, hand hygiene, and ventilation, and updating vaccination for inmates and staff. Visiting rights are temporarily suspended. First cases were confirmed after two testing rounds: 15 October saw 79 positives of 160 tested; 16–20 October added 29 positives from Lacen-GO testing, totaling 108, per SES-GO. The outbreak was notified on 14 October to the Strategic Information and Response Center in Vigilance (CIEVS Goiás), coordinating testing and care with the Southwest II Regional Health Team. Authorities are evaluating antiviral treatment needs and maintaining daily case monitoring. No deaths or hospitalizations due to severe respiratory illness have been reported; surveillance continues and visits will resume only after sanitary conditions are reassessed.

article.articleHeadline: Propolis Shows Antimicrobial Promise for Companion-Animal Skin Infections
article.articleSummary: Propolis shows in vitro antimicrobial activity against canine skin pathogens—Staphylococcus spp., Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Malassezia spp. and dermatophytes—but no controlled clinical trials exist for canine pyoderma, leaving its clinical value unproven as an antibiotic substitute. Across 18 studies, most work was laboratory-based; few small clinical assessments exist. Antimicrobial prescribing is high in companion animals: 29.2% of 2,599 dogs/cats across 52 practices received antibiotics; 25.7% of dog and 32.9% of cat consultations involved systemic therapy. S. pseudintermedius dominates canine pyoderma (~92% of cases), with up to 60% methicillin-resistant. External otitis isolates include P. aeruginosa (30.7%), S. pseudintermedius (25.1%), E. coli (19%); 47% are multidrug-resistant. Propolis composition is geography-dependent (Romania, Brazil, Argentina, Baltic region, Portugal, Turkey, Iraq); deep-eutectic-solvent extracts can be more potent than ethanolic, with MICs ~100–1,000 μg/mL vs 500–5,000 μg/mL. Active components include flavonoids and phenolic acids affecting membranes and efflux pumps.

article.articleHeadline: They guarantee supplies for malaria control in the jungle municipalities of Amazonas - MPPS
article.articleSummary: Malaria-control supplies and vaccines were distributed on Oct 24 to the jungle municipalities of Autana, Alto Orinoco, Atabapo, Manapiare, Maroa, and Río Negro in Amazonas state, Venezuela, to sustain malaria prevention, diagnosis and treatment in hard-to-reach communities. article.articleHeadline: Leptospirosis bacteria found in waterways, soil -- UP researchers
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-24, two peer-reviewed UPD-CS and Philippine Genome Center studies show Leptospira, the bacteria that cause leptospirosis, are present in urban waterways and soil, not only floodwaters. In Estero de Paco, a Metro Manila waterway, soil and water samples were collected from five sites and Leptospira were detected at all locations, indicating contamination across the entire system rather than a single hotspot. Senior author Windell Rivera notes that an entire connected waterway may function as a reservoir, requiring system-wide surveillance and interventions. The work also found Philippine Leptospira strains genetically distinct from previously sequenced strains. In a second study, researchers report the first genetic sequencing of Leptospira yasudae from the Philippines, representing only the 10th global sequence for the species and adding a Philippine reference to its genetic record.

Abdul-Aziz noted that the global eradication effort began after a 1979 Philippines vaccination project and expanded since 1988, reducing wild poliovirus from endemic in more than 120 countries to just Pakistan and Afghanistan remain endemic. The campaign emphasizes immunisation of children under public health guidelines and counters misconceptions that hinder vaccination, leveraging royal endorsement to overcome resistance.

Most cases are in people aged 65+, followed by 55–64 and 45–54. The region’s rainfall and flooding raise exposure to bacteria in soil and water. Transmission occurs via skin wounds, inhalation of dust, or ingestion of contaminated water/food. High‑risk groups include diabetics, kidney/liver/chronic lung disease patients, thalassemia, immunocompromised individuals, heavy drinkers, and farmers in frequent soil contact. Four preventive measures: avoid direct contact with soil/water; wear boots, gloves, long pants, and waterproof gear when exposure is necessary; wash and cover wounds immediately after exposure; drink clean water and ensure cooked food; seek medical care if fever persists after exposure or if respiratory symptoms/skin abscesses appear. Hotline 1422 for information.

The article notes that there is a vaccine for Japanese encephalitis; vaccination recommendations depend on destination, duration, and activities, and some countries mandate vaccination, France does not.
